one_month_reasoning: No scheduled company event before 2026-12-24 (Q4 FY27 print is due ~early March 2027). Window drivers: (a) post-earnings drift after an -18% print-day fall (218.37 -> 179.01, src 13) on a FY28 FTTH guide-down; DY's own 2018-19 guide-downs kept drifting lower over following weeks (src 11, 12); (b) sell-side target cuts and estimate revisions still to land (consensus feeds unrevised as of 2026-11-25, src 6/7), as after Q2 when KeyBanc/Cantor cut ~30% (src 10); (c) December tax-loss selling in a name down ~45% over the year; offsets: $200M buyback authorization and insider buying earlier in the fall (src 9), oversold bounce. Median set slightly below spot at $176 with sigma 0.175 (59%/3.5 = 0.169, nudged for fat tails).

model_inputs.structure_note: Annual driver-led set (not quarterly: a forecaster set for the supervisor, who rebuilds quarterly). Two reported segments (Communications, Building Systems) built from 5 drivers + depreciation; value carried by P/E on NTM adjusted EPS (0.7, ex intangible amortization like peer consensus, SBC through dilution) and LTM EV/EBITDA (0.3, mid-cycle cross-check). No DCF, no SOTP (both segments valued on the same contractor multiples).
model_inputs.gap_note: (1) Supplier-finance / factoring: playbook flags DY; the Q3 10-Q could not be fetched (SEC refused), so any supplier-finance or receivables-sale balance is NOT added to net debt; a $200M balance would cut ~$6/share. (2) Operating leases not in net debt (peers' EV on the same basis). (3) Two customers in distress (Q3 $22.7M reserve): further credit losses not modelled beyond the margin path. (4) Judgment calls for Kilian: P/E exit 11.35x via k=0.8 (k=1 gives ~-5% on the target); FY28 Comms growth 3.5% below the CEO's mid-single-digit statement. Financing: no equity raise expected (leverage 2.3x, buybacks ongoing), probability <10%.

downside.story: P10: FTTH customers cut FY28 builds further (core Comms -7% vs base), LH/DCI ramps slower, a data-center pause or local moratoria trims BS 12%, Comms margin -150bp on deleverage and more customer credit losses, BS margin -300bp; P/E de-rates ~3 turns toward DY's 2019 trough. base.story: FTTH dips in FY28 but long-haul/DCI (> $2B backlog) and Building Systems (+15%) keep revenue growing ~6%; Comms margin flat-to-up from 12.2%; EPS ~$19 FY28 / ~$22 FY29; the multiple stays well below peers (11.35x) after two guide resets.

upside.story: P90: FTTH pause is short, BEAD construction starts, LH/DCI converts faster, BS grows ~25%, Comms margin returns to ~13.2%; the multiple recovers ~2.5 turns toward the peer median.

reasoning: Base rates first: DY fell 18% on the print (218.37 -> 179.01) after an August reset (-21.6% in a week) and is 68% off its high. Its own precedent, the Aug-2018 and Feb-2019 guide-downs (stock $89 Jul-2018 -> $45 Feb-2019, still $44.5 Aug-2019, src 11, 12), shows reset contractors drifting lower for a year, so we keep 80% of today's discount (k=0.8, 11.35x NTM adj. EPS) instead of reverting to the 15.5x peer median, and the downside case puts the P/E ~3 turns lower. Fundamentals: Q3 beat on every line (revenue $2,056M, adj. EPS $5.23), backlog $12.9B with $6.7B in 12 months; the reset is FY28 FTTH. We build Comms core -1.5% in FY28 (below the CEO's mid-single-digit read), long-haul/DCI $550M from > $2B backlog, Building Systems +15% (labor-bound, below 'high teens or better'), Comms margin 12.4% (management says expansion), BS 19.5%. FY28 EPS ~$19.1 is at pre-revision consensus $18.99-20.11 that should fall post-print; FY29 ~$21.9 vs $22.37 consensus. Macro odds: Kalshi 2027 US recession 20% (src 20) and fed funds above 4% through Oct 2027 (src 14) keep the carriers' higher cost of capital (the reason the CEO gave for the FTTH slowdown) in place, which is why we do not model a quick FTTH re-acceleration. Net debt falls to ~$2.1B with Q4 seasonal cash and DSO normalization. Result: research target (12m) $250 (P/E $243, EV/EBITDA $267), P10 $119, P90 $380: a wide, slightly left-skewed band consistent with 59% realized vol. Research limited: the Q3 10-Q and 8-K exhibit could not be fetched from SEC (supplier-finance check open), and Twelve Data rate limits blocked the MasTec 2023 comparison price series.
